messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Multiple reports of TLS handshake failures and 5xx responses to api.redwood.ai originating at Cloudflare edge nodes. Alert threshold: 5% error rate over 5m. Investigate and acknowledge.

Dino-oncall: acked. I’m on it. seeing spike in 525/524 from synthetic monitors in us-east and eu-west. 

Amy-sre: I can reproduce from my laptop: curl https://api.redwood.ai/health —> hangs, then 525. Trying openssl to see handshake.

Amy-sre: ```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -debug
CONNECTED(00000003)
139816:errno=0
write to 0x7f...
140492873... SSL routines:tls_construct_client_hello:no protocols available
---
shutting down SSL
```

Ben-infra: that looks like Cloudflare terminating TLS upstream to us or failing during edge handshake. Our origin LB looks healthy. No spike on origin CPU or conns. Checking CF health: api backends show healthy in their dashboard.

Carla-support: we already have 8 customer tickets in the last 10m, many reporting timeouts and TLS errors. Estimated impact: ~12% error rate for paid API customers, some retries causing increased latency. Notifying CS leadership.

Dino-oncall: triage plan: 1) confirm it's CF edge problem vs origin 2) fail traffic to secondary POPs / route around problematic edges 3) open Cloudflare urgent ticket + provide PCAP/handshake logs 4) temporary mitigation (bypass CF for critical customers if needed).

Ben-infra: running mtr/traceroute from multiple vantage points. Observing consistent early TTL drop around Cloudflare ASN 13335 for affected traces. Running curl with --resolve to target origin LB directly (bypass CF)

Ben-infra: ```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:54.210.12.34 https://api.redwood.ai/health
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (54.210.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection established
* TLS handshake complete
{"status":"ok","version":"2026-03-15"}
```

Amy-sre: origin is fine. This is a Cloudflare/edge handshake failure. Posting initial diagnostics to the ticket.

Incident-bot: On-call handoff in 30m — please add notes to the incident channel and set owner.

Dino-oncall: @ben-infra take lead on mitigation and CF comms, I’ll coordinate customer updates and pagerota for escalation. @carla-support prep status message for customers (short outage note, ETA unknown).

Ben-infra: opened ticket with Cloudflare (Ticket #CF-209874). Provided sample openssl logs, traceroutes, and synthetic monitor timestamps. They responded: "we're investigating potential edge routing anomalies affecting handshake termination in N. America and EU regions."

Cloudflare-support: (external) Thanks for the data — we are seeing an internal BGP flap affecting some POPs. Eng team rolling mitigations. Can you confirm if bypassing Cloudflare via direct origin works? If so we can advise a temporary routing change while we remediate.

Dino-oncall: Can CF quantify impacted % of POPs or whether this will be a long remediation? Customers need an ETA.

Cloudflare-support: (external) Early estimate: partial POP-level impact, mitigations in progress, may take 15-45m to fully stabilize. We will update within 10m.

Carla-support: Posted initial customer-facing note to status with minimal details: "We are investigating connectivity issues affecting API reachability and TLS handshakes. Some requests may return 5xx errors. We will provide updates as we have them." :warning:

Amy-sre: For a faster mitigation we have two options: 1) temporarily lower DNS TTL and rotate CNAMEs to point to alternative Cloudflare-populated hostnames (risky) 2) temporary route for enterprise customers: publish direct origin IPs and whitelist Cloudflare fallback or clients. Which is viable?

Ben-infra: For scheduled enterprise customers we can patch WAF/ACL to allow direct origin and publish a short-lived endpoint (e.g., direct-api.redwood.ai) with strict rate limiting and auth. It’s a small blast radius. Start if CF advises longer outage.

Dino-oncall: hold on mitigation until CF update in 10m. We might not need risky DNS surgery. Meanwhile scale up retries and exponential backoff on gateway to reduce load from malformed retries.

Incident-bot: automated monitor: error rate peaked at 14% at 1815004380, currently steady at 9%.

Cloudflare-support: (external) Update: We've implemented route dampening on affected BGP peers; observing partial recovery. Handshake failure rate down ~60% in monitored regions. Continue to watch.

Amy-sre: I’m seeing some clients start to succeed again. Running global synthetic checks: us-east 90% success, eu-west 82%, ap-south 98% (unaffected).

Carla-support: CS ops: prioritizing highest-spend customers for direct outreach. Sending targeted emails and opening support DMs.

Dino-oncall: action items: 
- Ben: continue CF comms, gather packet captures and edge IPs for postmortem (assigned)
- Amy: collect synthetic metrics and baseline before incident (assigned)
- Carla: customer comms and open tickets list (assigned)
- Dino: incident owner, coordinate handoff in 25m and draft postmortem template

Ben-infra: CF just confirmed global backfill, handshake metrics improving. They’ll keep monitors on until next full propagation. Ticket updated.

Incident-bot: handoff notice: next on-call in 25 minutes. Please ensure runbook steps completed.

Dino-oncall: prepping brief for next oncall: cause appears to be Cloudflare BGP flap causing TLS handshake termination at some edges; origin unaffected. Root cause needs CF confirmation. No action required from customers at this time unless they see persistent failures.

Carla-support: added list of impacted customers to the ticket. Drafting follow-up note: "Issue resolved for most customers; Cloudflare applied mitigations. If you still experience TLS errors please reply and include your request IDs." :white_check_mark:

Amy-sre: recording timeframe: start ~1815004300, peak 1815004380, partial recovery 1815004800, stabilization 1815005920. Will add graphs and synthetic samples to the postmortem.

Ben-infra: closing provisional mitigation. CF will keep ticket open for 24h and provide final RCA.

Dino-oncall: closing incident channel for active coordination. Assign postmortem owner and timeline: draft in 48h, final RCA after CF report. Thanks all. :clap:

Incident-bot: Incident marked: mitigated. Creating postmortem card and assigning to Dino-oncall.

Carla-support: confirming customer communications queued. Will reopen if we get fresh reports.

Ben-infra: logs and traces archived to incidents bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1815004321-cf-bgp-handshake/

Amy-sre: adding checklist item for "edge provider routing alerts" to runbook to reduce MTTR next time.

Dino-oncall: good job. Closing thread.
